skill.name: ml-training-debugger
skill.description: Diagnose machine learning training failures, including loss divergence, mode collapse, gradient issues, architecture imbalance, optimization problems, and GPU memory errors.
skill.summary: Diagnose ML training failures with evidence-based root causes and prioritized fixes.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The static backtick and reconnaissance alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code formatting, and ML diagnostic wording. A separate semantic issue remains: the example agent configuration enables Bash despite describing the specialist as read-only.

remediation.issue: Bash is enabled for a workflow that is described as read-only.
remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash from allowed_tools, or require explicit user confirmation and a narrow allowlist for diagnostic commands.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger shell-backtick static alerts.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that fenced blocks are examples and avoid inline backticks around resources when plain text is enough.

semantic_findings.description: The skill configures the spawned specialist with allowed_tools including Bash while describing the agent as read-only. This creates a shell-execution path in a community diagnostic skill, even though the stated intent is passive analysis.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The SDK example explicitly includes Bash in allowed_tools next to Read and Grep. The surrounding text says the agent is read-only, so this is a capability exposure rather than proven malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Training failures are hard to debug when logs, curves, code, and configs point in different directions. This skill organizes the evidence and returns likely root causes, fixes, and verification steps.
actual_capabilities: Classifies training symptoms such as divergence, collapse, NaN loss, and stalled learning.
Reviews logs, loss curves, model code, configs, and error messages for diagnostic evidence.
Ranks likely root causes with confidence levels and supporting observations.
Suggests fixes for learning rates, gradients, architecture balance, and training loop issues.
Provides verification steps to confirm whether a proposed fix worked.
limitations: It depends on the quality and completeness of provided training artifacts.
It does not directly modify model code or training configs.
It cannot prove dataset quality issues without dataset access or representative samples.
Hardware-specific conclusions may need confirmation on the target training environment.

use_cases.title: Triage Failed Training Runs
use_cases.description: Identify why loss diverged, gradients exploded, or training stopped improving.

use_cases.title: Investigate Model Collapse
use_cases.description: Analyze repeated outputs, low diversity, or architecture imbalance before redesigning experiments.

use_cases.title: Debug Training Infrastructure Errors
use_cases.description: Review CUDA, checkpoint, dataloader, and framework errors from training logs.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Failed Run
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage with basic logs and symptoms.
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose my ML training run. Symptoms: [describe issue]. Logs: [paste key logs]. Config: [paste key settings]. Provide likely causes and fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Loss Divergence
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused analysis for unstable loss curves.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this loss divergence. Include the failure point, likely gradient or learning rate causes, supporting evidence, and a safe first fix.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Failure Hypotheses
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review when several causes are plausible.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these possible causes: [list causes]. Use my logs, gradients, model summary, and config to rank them by evidence and confidence.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Training System End to End
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced diagnosis across code, data flow, optimizer settings, and runtime errors.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform an end-to-end diagnosis of this training failure. Review logs, curves, architecture, optimizer setup, dataloader behavior, and hardware errors. Prioritize fixes.

output_examples.input: Loss was stable for six epochs, then jumped sharply at epoch seven with a gradient norm spike.
output_examples.output: Primary finding: learning rate or schedule transition likely caused gradient explosion. Recommended first fix: reduce learning rate, enable clipping, and monitor gradient norms.

output_examples.input: The model returns the same token for every prompt, but training loss still decreases.
output_examples.output: Primary finding: possible mode collapse or architecture imbalance. Review output diversity, embedding share, logit variance, and loss design before increasing training time.

output_examples.input: Training fails with CUDA memory errors after increasing batch size.
output_examples.output: Primary finding: memory pressure is likely from batch size, sequence length, or retained computation graphs. Try smaller batches, accumulation, and memory profiling.

best_practices: Provide logs, configs, loss curves, model summaries, and exact error messages together.
Ask for evidence-ranked causes before changing several parameters at once.
Verify each fix with one controlled rerun and tracked metrics.
anti_patterns: Do not request a diagnosis from only a vague symptom description.
Do not apply multiple high-impact fixes before measuring the first result.
Do not treat confidence scores as proof when key artifacts are missing.

faq.question: What artifacts should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide training logs, loss curves, config values, model code, and the exact error or warning text.

faq.question: Can it fix my training code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It diagnoses issues and recommends changes, but the skill states that code modification is outside its role.

faq.question: Does it work with PyTorch?
faq.answer: Yes. The prompt includes PyTorch and CUDA failure modes, including autograd, dataloader, checkpoint, and memory issues.

faq.question: Can it diagnose mode collapse?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews output diversity, logit behavior, architecture balance, and loss design for collapse symptoms.

faq.question: How does it handle uncertainty?
faq.answer: It should lower confidence, explain missing evidence, and request specific artifacts when the diagnosis is not supported.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production incidents?
faq.answer: It can help triage incidents, but critical changes should still follow your review, testing, and rollback process.
